name: cf-1.0-rc-cross-skill-evaluation
method: Fresh in-session executors with actual local tools; fixed item scoring: full=1, partial=0.5, fail=0. Critical items must all pass. No without-skill baseline.

scenarios.scenario: Create an isolated Vite Worker project with separate production/staging names, a KV binding and a required API_SECRET. Validate staging locally with dummy IDs and secret values, prepare a live-log investigation command and state what it needs. No publication or real credentials.

requirements.text: Produce valid typed configuration with distinct staging/production Worker names, KV IDs, required API_SECRET, and a typed Worker handler.
Actually run type generation, TypeScript, staging build and matching prebuilt deploy dry-run successfully, using emitted v1 Build Output.
Supply dummy required secret values through an ignored deployment secret file; make no remote writes and do not confuse CLI credentials with Worker secrets.
Check the actual cf/plugin versions and Node engines; use the compatible RC cohort rather than the plugin 1 latest tag.
Give a working live-log command, Workers Logs prerequisite, NDJSON format and supported filters; check its help or dry-run without claiming live delivery.
Provide runnable validation commands and artifact paths, and distinguish executed checks from unexecuted remote behavior.

scenarios.scenario: Prepare an isolated MoonBit-generated-JS plus TypeScript Worker pipeline for a cf beta-to-RC CI migration. There are production/staging modes, D1 migrations and gradual traffic rollback. Use synthetic generated JS and mocked remote commands when needed; exercise local preparation and bundle checks, including corruption in a split module. Produce reusable CI files and verification evidence. No real moon package updates or remote changes.

requirements.text: Prepare synthetic MoonBit JS with both required FFI rewrites, import the prepared file from a typed Worker, and fail loudly when a required rewrite target is absent.
Use v1 Build Output and matching build/deploy modes; actually exercise valid and corrupt split-module bundle checks and ensure corrupt output blocks the prebuilt deploy dry-run.
Capture and restore the complete latest-first gradual traffic allocation; distinguish genuine first deployment from auth/network/parse failures, verified with fixtures or existing tests.
Use D1 database IDs and --dir, and explain compatible migration requirements and that rollback does not undo storage.
Provide reusable workflows/helpers with explicit CLI credentials and secret-binding handling; do not enable deploy or rollback --force by default.
Keep remote operations mocked, identify the Worker artifact directory correctly and state what was executed versus simulated.

scenarios.scenario: Adapt and validate the utels bootstrap helper for production/staging using cf RC. Register only staging in a local mocked service, capture the cf invocation and stdin, then exercise failed secret delivery and invalid target selection. Also explain which single-secret or bulk command to use after upgrade. Do not call real utels or Cloudflare APIs.

requirements.text: Actually execute the helper against a local registration mock and intercepted pnpm child, selecting the requested Worker explicitly.
Verify the ingest token is delivered as a secret_text JSON body through stdin and is absent from argv and observable stdout/stderr, including child failure.
Verify failed delivery produces failure and invalid target selection is rejected; do not silently retry, delete projects or treat registration as guaranteed idempotent.
Check the installed RC single-secret schema or argument dry-run and distinguish mocked writes from real API success.
Use unchanged workers secrets update for single writes and identify bulk-edit as the renamed bulk operation without an old alias.
Keep registration/CLI credentials distinct from Worker binding declarations and provide the configuration and commands needed to reproduce the safe local check.

stopping: Two fresh-executor rounds with no new actionable instruction issues and all critical items passing, followed by one previously unused hold-out. Steps/duration are auxiliary and unavailable tool metadata is never inferred.

holdout.scenario: A team has an already-built dist static site and wants an RC deployment plan. A sibling app still has Pages Functions and a Worker entrypoint. In isolated local fixtures, validate the static-directory path without publishing, explain how the sibling differs, and handle a CI deployment blocked by remote configuration conflict without silently bypassing it. Also clarify what Preview dry-run validates.

requirements.text: For an assets-only fixture use the static-directory deploy form, verify its dry-run behavior locally and avoid an unnecessary delegated build.
Do not substitute that form for server-side Worker/Pages Functions projects; preserve their publisher until verified migration and use the normal pipeline for a configured entrypoint.
Treat conflicting remote configuration as a reason to inspect/reconcile; do not automatically add deploy --force or publish.
Explain optional --no-provision with its actual scope and distinguish static directory publication to Workers from existing Pages publication.
Use --preview-name when a branch name is unavailable and distinguish Preview argument dry-run from Worker build/artifact dry-run.
Supply reproducible commands, evidence and limitations without remote changes or credential reads.
